newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks notch up new intraday record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks notch up new intraday record.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed a slight intial slide to set to a new intraday record in quiet mid-morning trade Monday.
Traders said predictions for further cuts in primary rates on Tuesday were driving share prices.
The leading IPC index was up 16.53 points, or 0.43 percent, at 3,843.30 points.

Trading volume was light at 17.1 million shares. Open outcry was suspended for Monday's session and replaced with a screen trading system called SENTRA, due to U.S. markets being closed for Presidents Day.
Traders said demand for stocks had been carried over from Friday, and was notable in the case of holding company Femsa, up one peso at 28.50 pesos.
"Femsa had been hit very hard by the market, and had thus lagged behind recent gains," a desk trader said.
Dealers also drew attention to a recovery by media group Televisa and the retail sector.
Retail group Cifra B and C shares were the most traded stocks after Femsa.
"Also, stocks like Telmex and Grupo Carso CRAa1.MX are very firm," another trader said.
Other dealers said brokers were taking advantage of the absence of U.S. traders to raise share prices.
"It's easier to speculate when you counterparts are missing," one dealer said.
